title: Metabolism of Nucleic Acids
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Metabolism of Nucleic Acids curriculum: nucleotide structure, de novo purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis, salvage pathways, nucleotide interconversion, ribonucleotide reduction to deoxyribonucleotides, thymidylate synthesis, purine/pyrimidine catabolism (uric acid formation, gout, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome), and regulation. Scope is the metabolism/biosynthesis-and-breakdown of nucleotides, kept distinct from lipid/amino-acid/carbohydrate metabolism courses.

questions.question: A nucleotide is structurally composed of:
options: A nitrogenous base and a phosphate group only
A pentose sugar and a nitrogenous base only
A nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and one or more phosphate groups
Two nitrogenous bases joined by a phosphodiester bond
questions.correct_answer: A nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and one or more phosphate groups
questions.explanation: A nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) attached to a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) via an N-glycosidic bond, with one, two, or three phosphate groups esterified to the sugar's 5' carbon.

questions.question: The immediate activated form of ribose used in both de novo purine and pyrimidine nucleotide synthesis is:
questions.correct_answer: 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP)
questions.explanation: PRPP, formed from ribose-5-phosphate and ATP by PRPP synthetase, supplies the activated ribose-phosphate unit onto which purine bases are built de novo, and onto which pyrimidine bases are attached after ring formation.

questions.question: In de novo purine biosynthesis, the purine ring is built up step by step directly on:
options: Free purine base, later attached to ribose
PRPP itself, giving ribose-attached intermediates throughout
A pyrimidine ring that is later converted
questions.correct_answer: PRPP itself, giving ribose-attached intermediates throughout
questions.explanation: Unlike pyrimidine synthesis, de novo purine biosynthesis builds the purine ring atom-by-atom directly onto PRPP, so all intermediates from the first step (formation of 5-phosphoribosylamine) through IMP remain ribose-5-phosphate-linked.

questions.question: The first committed and rate-limiting step of de novo purine nucleotide synthesis, catalyzed by glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase, produces:
questions.correct_answer: 5-phosphoribosylamine
questions.explanation: Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase transfers an amide nitrogen from glutamine to PRPP, displacing pyrophosphate and forming 5-phosphoribosylamine; this is the committed, feedback-regulated first step of purine synthesis.

questions.question: The first purine nucleotide formed by the de novo pathway, from which both AMP and GMP are subsequently derived, is:
questions.correct_answer: Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
questions.explanation: The ten-step de novo purine pathway produces inosine monophosphate (IMP, the nucleotide of hypoxanthine) as the common branch-point precursor, which is then converted separately to AMP (via adenylosuccinate) and GMP (via xanthosine monophosphate).

questions.question: In contrast to purine biosynthesis, de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis differs in that:
options: The pyrimidine ring is fully assembled first (from carbamoyl phosphate and aspartate) and then attached to PRPP
It does not require PRPP at any stage
It uses glycine as the first ring atom, exactly as in purine synthesis
questions.correct_answer: The pyrimidine ring is fully assembled first (from carbamoyl phosphate and aspartate) and then attached to PRPP
questions.explanation: Pyrimidine synthesis first builds the six-membered orotate ring from carbamoyl phosphate and aspartate, and only afterward attaches it to PRPP (forming orotidine monophosphate), the reverse order from purine synthesis.

questions.question: The carbamoyl phosphate used in cytosolic de novo pyrimidine synthesis is produced by:
options: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I in mitochondria
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II in the cytosol, using glutamine as the nitrogen source
Aspartate transcarbamoylase directly from CO2 and ammonia
questions.correct_answer: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II in the cytosol, using glutamine as the nitrogen source
questions.explanation: Cytosolic carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS II) uses glutamine's amide nitrogen (unlike the mitochondrial urea-cycle CPS I, which uses free ammonia) to generate carbamoyl phosphate for pyrimidine synthesis.

questions.question: Aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), a classic allosteric enzyme, catalyzes condensation of carbamoyl phosphate with aspartate to form:
questions.correct_answer: Carbamoyl aspartate
questions.explanation: ATCase catalyzes the committed step of pyrimidine synthesis, joining carbamoyl phosphate and aspartate to form N-carbamoylaspartate, which is subsequently cyclized (by dihydroorotase) and oxidized to orotate.

questions.question: Orotate acquires its ribose-phosphate unit and is converted to uridine monophosphate (UMP) through the action of:
questions.correct_answer: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase, then orotidylate decarboxylase
questions.explanation: Orotate phosphoribosyltransferase attaches PRPP to orotate to form orotidine-5'-monophosphate (OMP), which orotidylate (OMP) decarboxylase then decarboxylates to yield UMP, the parent pyrimidine ribonucleotide.

questions.question: All other pyrimidine and purine ribo- and deoxyribonucleotides (di- and triphosphates) are ultimately derived from the monophosphates by:
options: Direct de novo synthesis of each nucleotide independently
Sequential phosphorylation by nucleoside monophosphate kinases and nucleoside diphosphate kinase
questions.correct_answer: Sequential phosphorylation by nucleoside monophosphate kinases and nucleoside diphosphate kinase
questions.explanation: Nucleoside monophosphates (e.g., UMP, AMP) are phosphorylated to diphosphates by specific NMP kinases, and diphosphates to triphosphates by the broadly specific nucleoside diphosphate kinase, using ATP as phosphate donor.

questions.question: The purine salvage pathway enzyme hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT) functions to:
options: Recycle free hypoxanthine and guanine bases back into nucleotides (IMP and GMP) using PRPP
questions.correct_answer: Recycle free hypoxanthine and guanine bases back into nucleotides (IMP and GMP) using PRPP
questions.explanation: HGPRT salvages free purine bases released from nucleotide turnover, reattaching them to PRPP to regenerate IMP (from hypoxanthine) or GMP (from guanine), sparing the energetically costly de novo pathway.

questions.question: A near-total deficiency of HGPRT causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, characterized by hyperuricemia together with:
options: Compulsive self-injurious behaviour, choreoathetosis, and intellectual disability
questions.correct_answer: Compulsive self-injurious behaviour, choreoathetosis, and intellectual disability
questions.explanation: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, an X-linked disorder from HGPRT deficiency, causes excess purine degradation to uric acid (gout, urate nephropathy) plus a distinctive neurological/behavioural phenotype including self-mutilation and choreoathetosis.

questions.question: In humans, the end product of purine catabolism, excreted in urine, is:
questions.correct_answer: Uric acid
questions.explanation: Humans lack uricase, so purine catabolism (of adenine and guanine, via hypoxanthine/xanthine) terminates at uric acid, which is excreted in urine; many other mammals possess uricase and further degrade it to the more soluble allantoin.

questions.question: Xanthine oxidase, the enzyme inhibited by the anti-gout drug allopurinol, catalyzes the conversion of:
options: Hypoxanthine to xanthine, and xanthine to uric acid
questions.correct_answer: Hypoxanthine to xanthine, and xanthine to uric acid
questions.explanation: Xanthine oxidase catalyzes both terminal oxidation steps of purine catabolism (hypoxanthine to xanthine, then xanthine to uric acid); allopurinol, a hypoxanthine analogue, inhibits this enzyme, lowering uric acid production in gout.

questions.question: Gout results from the deposition of needle-shaped crystals of which substance in joints, causing acute inflammatory arthritis?
questions.correct_answer: Monosodium urate
questions.explanation: Gout is caused by hyperuricemia leading to precipitation of monosodium urate crystals in joints (classically the first metatarsophalangeal joint), triggering an acute inflammatory response.

questions.question: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, which causes severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), leads to immune cell toxicity because:
options: Deoxyadenosine and dATP accumulate to toxic levels, inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase and impairing lymphocyte DNA synthesis
Uric acid production stops entirely, starving cells of purines
Guanine accumulates and is directly cytotoxic
questions.correct_answer: Deoxyadenosine and dATP accumulate to toxic levels, inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase and impairing lymphocyte DNA synthesis
questions.explanation: Without ADA to deaminate deoxyadenosine, it is phosphorylated to dATP, which accumulates especially in lymphocytes and allosterically inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, blocking deoxyribonucleotide production needed for lymphocyte proliferation, producing SCID.

questions.question: Deoxyribonucleotides required for DNA synthesis are formed from ribonucleotides by direct reduction of the 2'-hydroxyl of the ribose, catalyzed by:
questions.correct_answer: Ribonucleotide reductase
questions.explanation: Ribonucleotide reductase converts ribonucleoside diphosphates (NDPs) directly to the corresponding 2'-deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs), the committed step supplying precursors for DNA replication and repair.

questions.question: Ribonucleotide reductase uses electrons ultimately supplied by NADPH, delivered through a small protein cofactor called:
questions.correct_answer: Thioredoxin (or glutaredoxin)
questions.explanation: Thioredoxin (regenerated by thioredoxin reductase using NADPH), or alternatively glutaredoxin, supplies the reducing equivalents that ribonucleotide reductase uses to reduce the ribose 2'-OH to a deoxyribose.

questions.question: Thymidylate synthase converts dUMP to dTMP using which one-carbon donor?
questions.correct_answer: N5,N10-methylenetetrahydrofolate
questions.explanation: Thymidylate synthase methylates dUMP to dTMP, transferring and reducing a one-carbon unit from N5,N10-methylenetetrahydrofolate, which is oxidized to dihydrofolate in the process.

questions.question: Dihydrofolate reductase regenerates tetrahydrofolate from dihydrofolate after the thymidylate synthase reaction, and is the target of which anticancer/antifolate drug?
questions.correct_answer: Methotrexate
questions.explanation: Methotrexate, a folate analogue, competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, preventing regeneration of tetrahydrofolate and thus blocking thymidylate (and purine) synthesis, which is exploited to kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.

questions.question: 5-Fluorouracil, an anticancer drug, exerts its effect on nucleotide metabolism mainly by:
options: Being converted to F-dUMP, which forms an irreversible covalent complex with thymidylate synthase and folate, inhibiting the enzyme
questions.correct_answer: Being converted to F-dUMP, which forms an irreversible covalent complex with thymidylate synthase and folate, inhibiting the enzyme
questions.explanation: 5-Fluorouracil is converted intracellularly to fluorodeoxyuridine monophosphate (F-dUMP), a suicide substrate that traps thymidylate synthase in an inactive ternary complex with the folate cofactor, blocking dTMP (and thus DNA) synthesis.

questions.question: Pyrimidine catabolism (of cytosine, uracil, and thymine) differs from purine catabolism in that the pyrimidine ring is:
options: Opened and degraded to soluble products such as beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate, which enter general metabolism
questions.correct_answer: Opened and degraded to soluble products such as beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate, which enter general metabolism
questions.explanation: Unlike purines, which yield the poorly soluble uric acid, pyrimidine rings are reduced and opened during catabolism to highly soluble products (beta-alanine from cytosine/uracil, beta-aminoisobutyrate from thymine) that feed into other metabolic pathways, so pyrimidine catabolism rarely causes disease.

questions.question: In humans, the pathway of purine nucleotide degradation of AMP proceeds through which base before forming uric acid?
questions.correct_answer: Hypoxanthine
questions.explanation: AMP is deaminated (directly or via adenosine) to IMP/inosine and then to the free base hypoxanthine, which xanthine oxidase oxidizes to xanthine and then uric acid.

questions.question: The committed, rate-limiting step of de novo purine biosynthesis (glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase) is feedback-inhibited allosterically by:
options: IMP, AMP, and GMP (the pathway's end products)
questions.correct_answer: IMP, AMP, and GMP (the pathway's end products)
questions.explanation: Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase is allosterically inhibited by the purine nucleotide end products IMP, AMP, and GMP, providing classic feedback regulation that matches purine synthesis to cellular need.

questions.question: In de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis, the mammalian regulatory enzyme most sensitive to feedback inhibition by the end product UTP (or CTP) is:
options: Aspartate transcarbamoylase / the CPS II component of the CAD complex
questions.correct_answer: Aspartate transcarbamoylase / the CPS II component of the CAD complex
questions.explanation: In mammals, carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (part of the trifunctional CAD complex, which also includes aspartate transcarbamoylase) is allosterically inhibited by UTP and activated by PRPP, providing the main feedback control point of the pyrimidine pathway.

questions.question: Adenine, guanine, and cytosine can all be classified biochemically as derivatives of which parent heterocyclic ring system(s)?
options: Adenine and guanine from purine; cytosine from pyrimidine
Adenine from pyrimidine; guanine and cytosine from purine
questions.correct_answer: Adenine and guanine from purine; cytosine from pyrimidine
questions.explanation: Adenine and guanine are purines (fused imidazole-pyrimidine bicyclic rings); cytosine, along with thymine and uracil, is a pyrimidine (single six-membered ring).

questions.question: Uracil is the pyrimidine base characteristic of RNA, whereas DNA instead contains:
questions.correct_answer: Thymine (5-methyluracil) in its place
questions.explanation: DNA uses thymine (5-methyluracil) instead of the uracil found in RNA; thymine is formed by methylation of dUMP by thymidylate synthase, providing a distinguishing, more chemically stable base for the genetic material.

questions.question: Ribonucleotide reductase activity, and hence deoxyribonucleotide supply, rises sharply during which phase of the cell cycle?
options: S phase, coinciding with active DNA replication
questions.correct_answer: S phase, coinciding with active DNA replication
questions.explanation: Ribonucleotide reductase expression and activity peak in S phase, when cells actively replicate DNA and therefore require a large, balanced supply of all four deoxyribonucleotides.

questions.question: Hydroxyurea, used clinically (e.g., in sickle cell disease and some leukemias), acts on nucleotide metabolism by:
options: Inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase by scavenging the tyrosyl free radical required for its activity
questions.correct_answer: Inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase by scavenging the tyrosyl free radical required for its activity
questions.explanation: Hydroxyurea quenches the tyrosyl radical essential for the catalytic mechanism of ribonucleotide reductase, blocking deoxyribonucleotide production and thereby inhibiting DNA synthesis.

questions.question: Orotic aciduria, an inherited disorder of pyrimidine metabolism, results from a deficiency of the bifunctional enzyme UMP synthase (orotate phosphoribosyltransferase / orotidylate decarboxylase), causing:
options: Megaloblastic anemia and excess urinary orotic acid, unresponsive to vitamin B12
Excess uric acid crystal deposition in joints
questions.correct_answer: Megaloblastic anemia and excess urinary orotic acid, unresponsive to vitamin B12
questions.explanation: Hereditary orotic aciduria impairs conversion of orotate to UMP, causing orotate accumulation and excretion plus a megaloblastic anemia (due to impaired pyrimidine, hence nucleic acid, synthesis) that does not respond to B12 or folate, but improves with uridine supplementation.

questions.question: Adenosine phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT), analogous to HGPRT but specific for adenine, salvages free adenine base by combining it with PRPP to regenerate:
questions.correct_answer: AMP
questions.explanation: APRT catalyzes the salvage reaction adenine + PRPP → AMP + PPi, recycling free adenine (released during nucleic acid/nucleotide turnover) directly back into the adenine nucleotide pool.

questions.question: Compared with de novo nucleotide synthesis, salvage pathways are metabolically advantageous mainly because they:
options: Use far less ATP/energy than building nucleotides from simple precursors
Are the only pathways capable of producing purines in humans
Produce nucleotides with different bases than de novo synthesis
questions.correct_answer: Use far less ATP/energy than building nucleotides from simple precursors
questions.explanation: Salvage pathways recycle preformed bases and nucleosides released from nucleic acid turnover, bypassing the many ATP- and amino-acid-consuming steps of de novo synthesis, making them energetically far cheaper, especially important in tissues like brain and erythrocytes with limited de novo capacity.
